title: SAC: Disaggregated KV Cache System for Sparse Attention LLMs with CXL
event_hint: Research paper presents SAC, the first CXL-based disaggregated KV cache system for sparse attention LLMs
problem: Sparse attention LLMs only utilize a small fraction of KV entries per layer (top-k), but traditional RDMA-based disaggregated memory systems perform coarse-grained full prefix KV cache fetching. This causes two fundamental bottlenecks: (P1) Transmission bottleneck with latency growing near-linearly with concurrency and context length, and (P2) Local memory wasting where only 21% of KV cache is utilized in 128K-context scenarios
mechanism: SAC leverages CXL's cache-line granularity load/store semantics (near-DRAM access latency with zero message protocol overhead) to fetch only required top-k KV entries on demand during inference. Integrates with SGLang HiSparse framework and uses CXL memory pool with multiple CXL-MEM devices interconnected via CXL switch. CXL provides hardware-managed load/store memory semantic at cache-line granularity, achieving remote memory access latencies approaching local DRAM

evidence.claim: SAC achieves 2.1x higher throughput compared to RDMA-based disaggregated memory pool
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 serving, context lengths 16K-128K tokens, integrated with SGLang

evidence.claim: SAC achieves 9.7x lower Time to First Token (TTFT) compared to RDMA-based disaggregated memory pool
SAC achieves 1.8x lower Time Between Tokens (TBT) compared to RDMA-based disaggregated memory pool
SAC incurs only 9% throughput degradation compared to non-disaggregated upper bound
CXL read latency for sparse KV access ranges from 1.04x to 1.64x of DRAM, while RDMA ranges from 3.97x to 19.7x of DRAM
evidence.condition: Sparse KV cache retrieval with varying number of fetched indices (64-2048)

evaluation_context: Integrated into SGLang serving framework and evaluated on DeepSeek-V3.2 model end-to-end serving across context lengths from 16K to 128K tokens. System topology includes CXL memory pool with multiple CXL-MEM devices interconnected via CXL switch, PCIe 5.0 x16 links (64 GB/s per link)
limitations: Evaluation limited to DeepSeek-V3.2 sparse attention model; other sparse architectures (GLM-5.1, DeepSeek-V4) mentioned but not benchmarked. Hardware topology assumes CXL 2.0/3.0 switch availability; deployment constraints in existing datacenters not discussed
project_relevance: Directly relevant to memory semantics and DSA offloading专题: addresses memory resource disaggregation with new access semantics (CXL load/store at cache-line granularity), demonstrates reduction in memory bandwidth pressure and transmission bottlenecks. Shows end-to-end application benefits (2.1x throughput, 9.7x TTFT). Should be categorized under 'memory_semantics' direction
